opening_message:
Ticket 1: Matthew Mejia (employee ID E034) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E034.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Matthew Mejia (E034) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires role ownership of the system, which does not apply here. Requested write is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security check: E034 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training limits the max to read. Requested write is above the max, so recommend read.
reason: Ticket E034 requests write access to Payroll. The two notes conflict: HR's note says Matthew Mejia is full-time (max write, so write would be allowed), while Security's note says he is a contractor with only basic security training (max read, so write would be above max). Because the facts conflict and the more restrictive interpretation (contractor with basic training) caps access at read, granting read is the only level valid under both interpretations. I grant read.
